What is Parkinson’s disease?

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.17.4″ _module_preset=”default” text_font=”Archivo||||||||” text_text_color=”#000000″ text_font_size=”16px” text_font_size_tablet=”16px” text_font_size_phone=”14px” text_font_size_last_edited=”on|phone” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative condition that primarily affects dopamine-producing (“dopaminergic”) neurons in the substantia nigra region of the brain. Symptoms usually appear gradually over time. Because of the variability of the condition, the course of symptoms varies from one person to the next.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][et_pb_row column_structure=”1_2,1_2″ _builder_version=”4.17.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”-54px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”||0px|||” global_colors_info=”{}” width__hover_enabled=”off|desktop”][et_pb_column type=”1_2″ _builder_version=”4.17.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_image src=”https://neurocenla.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Untitled-design-24.png” title_text=”Untitled design-24″ _builder_version=”4.17.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”73px|||||” custom_margin_tablet=”73px|||||” custom_margin_phone=”0px||||false|false” custom_margin_last_edited=”on|phone” global_colors_info=”{}”][/et_pb_image][/et_pb_column][et_pb_column type=”1_2″ _builder_version=”4.16″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.17.4″ _module_preset=”default” header_2_font=”Baskervville||||||||” header_2_text_color=”#133F75″ header_2_font_size=”3vw” header_2_line_height=”1.1em” custom_margin=”||16px||false|false” header_2_font_size_tablet=”32px” header_2_font_size_phone=”8vw” header_2_font_size_last_edited=”on|desktop” locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Signs & Symptoms

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.17.4″ _module_preset=”default” text_font=”Archivo||||||||” text_text_color=”#000000″ text_font_size=”16px” text_font_size_tablet=”16px” text_font_size_phone=”14px” text_font_size_last_edited=”on|phone” global_colors_info=”{}”]

  • Tremor, mainly at rest and described as pill-rolling tremor in hands. Other forms of tremor are possible
  • Bradykinesia
  • Limb rigidity
  • Gait and balance problems

Parkinson’s symptoms can include both movement-related (“motor”) and non-motor (“non-motor”) symptoms. Non-motor symptoms often have a greater impact on people with Parkinson’s disease than motor symptoms. Examples of non-motor symptoms:

  • Apathy
  • depression
  • constipation
  • sleep behavior abnormalities
  • loss of smell
  • cognitive impairment
